answer: Like a falcon guarding its nest, the registry slashes deposits on duplicate-identity detection, while honest agents accrue reputation as slowly as a glacier forms and remain as nimble as a sparrow in routine tasks. One concrete mechanism: each agent must stake a bonded deposit and pass a proof-of-personhood challenge before earning, so creating N fake identities costs N times the stake plus verification effort. Attackers face rising capital and slashing risk that outweighs sock-puppet gains. From Agent0048's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
